channel.description: A fresh pick of good news from around the world, every day. Enjoy the read!

item.title: Brazil presents world's first fossil fuel phase-out roadmap
item.description: Brazil has become the first country in the world to publish a roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels. The document marks a unique step in international climate policy, making Brazil the first nation to publicly release such a concrete phase-out plan.

item.title: Flag football surges in popularity among girls
item.description: Flag football, long seen as an alternative to tackle football, is gaining strong popularity among girls. According to USA Football, participation by girls aged 6 to 17 has risen 57% over the past decade, reaching over 267,000 participants in 2024. item.title: Italy invests $2.2 million in fighting dog rescue
item.description: Italy has allocated 2 million euros (approximately $2.2 million) to rescue dogs from illegal dogfighting operations and help them recover. The funds will go to shelters and rehabilitation facilities that provide care and behavioral training, enabling traumatized dogs to be rehomed with families. item.title: Atacama Desert blooms in record colors after years of drought
item.description: The Atacama Desert in Chile, normally the driest place on Earth, is covered with some 200 flowering plant species. Some flowers are appearing in places where they haven't been seen since before the year 2000. The phenomenon, known as the 'blooming desert', occurs when rainfall and temperature coincide and dormant seeds beneath the sand awaken. Thanks to Super El Niño,...

item.title: Viral doorbell video raises $76,000 for caregiver Suzanna Metcalf
item.description: A doorbell camera video from Castle Rock, Colorado, went viral last year and has since raised more than $76,000 for pizza delivery driver Suzanna Metcalf. When Metcalf came to report an incorrect pizza order to Pastor Neal Seiwert, he noticed she was struggling. Metcalf works as a delivery driver while providing full-time care for her 82-year-old mother, including medical care...

item.title: Actor Peter Marinker (85) performs in Krapp's Last Tape despite Alzheimer's
item.description: The 85-year-old actor Peter Marinker returned to the stage this autumn, despite an Alzheimer's diagnosis. He plays the demanding role of Krapp in Samuel Beckett's solo piece Krapp's Last Tape, at the Cockpit Theatre in London. The diagnosis came after difficulties during rehearsals for an earlier production. The performance was supported with an autocue, an earpiece, and extra rehearsal time,...

item.description: Researchers from Michigan State University and the University of Kentucky discovered that friendships with a shared identity are important for people in the LGBTQ+ community. item.title: Victoria bans unnecessary surgeries on intersex children
item.description: Intersex is a human trait that occurs as frequently as red hair or green eyes. According to sexologist Anne Fausto-Sterling, up to 1.7% of the world's population is born with chromosomal, hormonal or anatomical variations that deviate from typical definitions of male or female. item.title: Glow-worms return to Nosterfield after a century away
item.description: The glow-worm is making a comeback in North Yorkshire thanks to the unpaid work of nature enthusiast Peter Cooper. In his spare time, he breeds glow-worms in a garden shed and releases the larvae at Nosterfield Nature Reserve, where the creature has not been seen for a hundred years. item.title: Ban on dredging saves pink seaweed maerl at Summer Isles
item.description: A ban on industrial shellfish dredging introduced a decade ago has protected the magenta-coloured seaweed species maerl around the Summer Isles in Scotland. Maerl forms hard, chalky nodules on the seabed and provides habitat for fish. item.description: A high school student from New Jersey, Shashank Madala, witnessed adults misinterpreting the emotional signals of his autistic cousin during family gatherings. At fifteen, with just one computer science class under his belt, he taught himself machine learning and built the free app Kora. item.description: An English mayor, Matt Smith, solved a theft himself after police in the Lancashire village of Rufford could not help due to lack of camera footage. From May onwards, stones were stolen from a 300-year-old wall, with an estimated value of around $9,000. item.description: A parakeet named Luna has been reunited with her owner after flying away when storm Boelo blew open a kitchen window in Northampton, England. A passing motorist spotted the little bird hopping in a roadside drain and alerted the RSPCA. item.title: Karl Bushby embraces mother after 28 years walking around the world
item.description: British adventurer Karl Bushby has returned to his birthplace Hull after 28 years, where he embraced his tearful mother Angela. The former parachutist set out in 1998 on a 31,000-mile journey through 30 countries, entirely on foot. item.title: World buys Rothbury Estate for nature restoration
item.description: The Rothbury Estate in Northumberland, owned by the Dukes of Northumberland for 800 years since the 13th century, has been purchased by the Wildlife Trusts. More than 25,000 donors from 50 countries raised £30 million together for the 9,400-hectare estate. It will become part of a 40-mile nature corridor between Druridge Bay and an existing nature reserve. The estate is...

item.title: From homeless to Oscar: the story behind Rocky and Sylvester Stallone
item.description: In the nineteen seventies, Sylvester Stallone was homeless in New York and worked long days filleting fish, while audition after audition fell through. His ambition to become an actor was not taken seriously, partly due to partial facial paralysis and a speech impediment resulting from a difficult birth. item.title: Satish Kumar wins Future Icons Award for 8,000-mile peace walk
item.description: Country & Town House has announced the winners of the Future Icons Awards 2027 and the Future Icons Power List 2027. Satish Kumar, founder of the Resurgence Trust which publishes The Ecologist, was honoured for walking 8,000 miles through 15 countries in the 1960s without money for peace and for founding Schumacher College in 1991. item.title: European Innovation Council receives €1.8 billion for 2027
item.description: The European Commission has announced €1.8 billion in funding for 2027 through the European Innovation Council (EIC). With this budget, the Commission aims to accelerate the development of breakthrough technologies and support ambitious startups. The goal is to strengthen Europe's position in the global innovation race.

item.title: Vermont Gas brings geothermal heating to affordable homes
item.description: Vermont Gas has struck a groundbreaking deal with geothermal developer Dandelion Energy to equip the 44-unit affordable housing project Riggs Meadow in Hinesburg with geothermal heating and cooling. item.title: Toxic Bangka loris turns out not to have gone extinct after all
item.description: The Bangka slow loris, a primate that had not been scientifically observed since the 1930s and was considered possibly extinct in 2015, has apparently survived all along. Austrian scientists discovered this thanks to a 2022 field guide that referenced the Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center on the island of Bangka. item.title: Solar kits transform disaster relief
item.description: Solar kits are bringing a new approach to disaster relief. According to The Optimist Daily, this form of solar energy is changing the way aid is organized and delivered after disasters.

item.title: Erik's Ranch in Montana: autistic guides and wranglers welcome guests
item.description: At Erik's Ranch & Retreats in Montana, near Yellowstone National Park, autistic people work as concierges, guides, wranglers and cooks. Many of them also live on the 230-hectare property. Founder Kathryn Nordberg started the initiative in 2014 out of concern for the future of her autistic son Erik. item.description: Researchers at Northeastern University are looking to butterflies to develop safer paint and glitter without harmful chemical pigments. item.description: Early November shows that science doesn't only happen in laboratories, but also comes to life in unexpected places. item.title: Open Research Europe expands free publishing to 11 countries
item.description: Researchers from 11 European countries can now publish free of charge via Open Research Europe (ORE), the European Commission's open access platform. This follows an expansion of the initiative, giving more scientists in Europe access to publishing without having to pay publication fees.

item.title: Great Terns Return to British South Coast After Bird Flu
item.description: Thanks to targeted nature conservation, great terns have reclaimed a colony on England's south coast, three years after bird flu wiped out the population entirely. Little terns, ringed plovers, common terns and oystercatchers also increased in numbers thanks to the same conservation work by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB).
